takes.overview: The draft room went sideways but the roster didn't: second-strongest team on paper, built on the D corps (Seider, Bouchard, Clarke, Chychrun all top-40 D by ROS) that this blocks-heavy scoring rewards. The soft spot is the back half of the forwards - Zacha, Laferriere and McKenna are below a typical league starter, so forward depth is where every waiver dollar and trade chip should go. Goalies are fine for now at 0.1 per save, but Hellebuyck's suspension is the one thing to watch this week.
takes.matchup: Week 1 is a 13-day opener and Angie's has about 12 more projected starts, which is the whole gap. You can't fix schedule volume with lineup tweaks alone - the fastest lever is swapping a low-game forward for a free agent whose team plays 6-7 times in the window.
takes.roster: Hold all four top D - they're the edge. Bedard is on IR, so his slot costs you nothing yet. Hellebuyck is starting in G while listed SUSPENSION: confirm his status before each game and slide Greaves in if he's out.
takes.free_agents: The model wants a forward (Hartman, Frondell, Cuylle) for Swayman. I'd make that move with Zacha or Laferriere as the drop instead while Hellebuyck's suspension is unresolved - keep three goalies until you know how many games he misses.
takes.trades: Matt's Monstrous Team is the natural partner: they're thin on D and deep at forward. Clarke for Jason Robertson is the cleanest ask (+22 ROS for you, they still gain a little). Don't sell Seider or Bouchard for forwards - the D gap to replacement is bigger here than the F gap.
